name: make-a-skill
query: I keep walking you through the same five steps to set up a new project. Can you turn that into a skill?
why: The canonical authoring request. Creating a skill from a repeated procedure is this skill's core job, and the house profile (frontmatter fields, description discipline, structure) has to load before any file is written.

name: skill-never-fires
query: My skill almost never loads when I actually need it. What is wrong with it?
why: Trigger debugging. The answer is description discipline - when-to-fire conditions, situation clauses over phrase lists, and explicit invocation as the fallback - which lives only in this skill.

name: which-shape
query: Should this be a skill, a slash command, or a subagent?
why: The shape decision is named explicitly in the description. Choosing between the four artifact types is authoring, not use.

name: frontmatter-field-validity
query: Can I put a version field at the top level of the frontmatter, or does that break anything?
why: Frontmatter validity against the open standard plus the Claude Code extension set. The house answer is no top-level custom keys and no version numbers at all, which nothing else in the repo states.

name: audit-the-skills
query: Go through everything in the skills directory and tell me which ones are off convention.
why: The audit checklist. Structure, name-matches-directory, description length, reference depth and advisory-agent tool allowlists are all this skill's items.

name: add-a-subagent
query: Add an agent definition that can only read and trace call sites, nothing that writes.
why: Subagent authoring. The read-only tools allowlist requirement lives here, and capability gates behavior while prose does not.

name: enforcement-placement
query: I want the agent stopped from writing into this directory. Where does that rule actually belong?
why: Rules and hooks placement. Enforcement goes in a PreToolUse hook or the permission system rather than prose, and hook exit code 2 blocks while exit 1 does not.

name: body-too-long
query: This SKILL.md is up to 700 lines and getting unwieldy. Sort it out.
why: Structure rules - body under 500 lines, overflow into references one level deep, tables of contents on long reference files.

name: write-eval-cases
query: This skill has no eval cases at all. Write some so I can tell whether it fires.
why: The eval convention: triggers.json versus evals.json, which consumer reads which schema, both polarities, and the invocation gotchas for run_eval.py.

name: using-a-skill
query: Use the statistics skill on this A/B test result and tell me if the difference is real.
why: Invoking a skill, not authoring one. Belongs to statistics; this skill owns the file, never the subject matter inside it.

name: reading-a-skills-content
query: What does the machine-learning skill say about handling class imbalance?
why: A question answered by the skill's content. Belongs to machine-learning. Naming a skill file is not an authoring request.

name: general-coding
query: Refactor this Python function so it takes a config object instead of six positional arguments.
why: Ordinary code work with no agent-tooling artifact involved. Guards against firing on anything that mentions editing a file.

name: hidden-instruction-scan
query: Someone sent me this skill file. Check it for hidden instructions before I commit it.
why: Belongs to my-security-review-checklist, which owns the hidden-character scan. The object is a skill file, which makes this the hardest false positive: authoring owns the shape of the file, the security gate owns what is smuggled inside it.

name: slop-cleanup-of-a-skill
query: This SKILL.md reads like a bot wrote it. Strip out the filler and the meta-commentary.
why: Belongs to ai-slop-magic-eraser. Same file type, different concern - prose quality is its own gate, and this skill only requires that the gate was run.

name: parallel-work-on-skills
query: Spawn three workers to update these skills at the same time.
why: Belongs to meta-loop. Orchestration vocabulary plus skill-shaped objects, but the request is about how the work is delegated, not about what makes a skill correct.

name: push-the-finished-skill
query: The skill is done, push it up.
why: Belongs to repo-device-sync, which owns any push intent however casually phrased.
